# Reader Guide and Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

*Physical AI Systems* is written as an independent, self-contained textbook for advanced undergraduate students, graduate researchers, and practicing systems engineers who wish to build machines that safely couple learned intelligence to physical matter and energy.

Readers arrive from different engineering disciplines, with the primary audience being computer science and electrical engineering students with a strong background in Machine Learning Systems. This guide delineates the assumed technical baseline from material developed within this book, and outlines reading pathways tailored to different engineering backgrounds.

## The Technical Starting Point {#sec-prereq-baseline}

The curriculum is designed for readers transitioning from digital computing disciplines into physical embodiment. The primary audience arrives with deep fluency in machine learning systems, computer architecture, and software engineering. This book systematically establishes the physical principles and safety architectures required to bridge digital intelligence and physical execution.

### What the machine learning systems student brings

Readers emerging from modern machine learning systems curricula—such as the CS 288 sequence or the first three volumes of this series—bring four critical engineering competencies:

* **Deep Learning Frameworks and Computational Graphs**: Mastery of PyTorch and JAX tensor operations, automatic differentiation (autograd reverse-mode graph construction), operator scheduling, and common neural architectures (Transformers, multi-head attention, convolutional vision backbones, and diffusion or flow-matching decoders). Readers understand operator fusion and compiler toolchains (such as TorchDynamo, Accelerated Linear Algebra (XLA), and Triton).
* **Computer Architecture and Accelerator Memory Hierarchies**: Deep understanding of modern processor and accelerator hierarchies: general-purpose CPUs, discrete GPUs, and dedicated neural processing units (NPUs). Readers know how to profile execution using the Roofline model, distinguishing compute-bound kernels from memory-bandwidth-bound operations across on-chip SRAM, low-power DDR (LPDDR), and high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
* **Distributed Systems and Concurrency**: Working knowledge of distributed training and inference clusters, collective communication primitives (AllReduce, AllGather, ReduceScatter), tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and low-latency interconnects. Readers are experienced with concurrent programming, asynchronous event loops, inter-process communication, and systems programming in C or C++.
* **Digital Systems Assumptions**: Familiarity with software abstractions where hardware is treated as an infinitely compliant execution engine, batch throughput is maximized, execution is asynchronous and speculative, and runtime errors are safely caught and resolved through software exceptions, retry loops, and checkpoint rollbacks.

### What you will master: The physical AI frontier

Physical AI terminates digital software forgiveness. When a learned policy issues commands across the causal boundary into physical actuators, the machine encounters constraints that cannot be solved by expanding model capacity or training datasets. This textbook develops the physical, computational, and architectural principles required to master these realities:

* **Continuous Plant Dynamics and Reflected Inertia**: Newton's second law ($F = ma$, $\tau = I \alpha$), multi-body rigid dynamics, gearbox compliance, backlash, and reflected rotor inertia ($J_{\text{ref}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$), revealing why high gear ratios cause motor inertia to dominate joint acceleration (@sec-body).
* **The Unified Stopping Distance Budget**: Unifying optical sensor exposure, SerDes transport latency, heterogeneous memory crossbar contention, neural inference tail latency, fieldbus jitter, and mechanical brake actuation into a single spatial stopping budget ($d_{\text{stop}} \approx v \tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{brake}}}$), where computational delay translates directly into physical stopping distance (@sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-nervous).
* **Power Electronics and Thermal Dissipation**: Three-phase inverter bridge topologies, pulse-width modulation (PWM) gate drivers, phase current limits, irreversible Joule heating in motor windings ($P = I_{\text{phase}}^2 R_{\text{phase}}$), thermal time constants ($\Delta T = P \cdot R_{\text{th}}$), and power delivery network (PDN) voltage droop under transient torque loads (@sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-placement).
* **Endogenous Data and Closed-Loop Distribution Shift**: Formulating training, data collection, and evaluation for systems whose own actions dictate future sensory observations ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$). Readers will analyze why batching across time is impossible, how imitation learning errors compound quadratically over the planning horizon ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$, @sec-boundary-bedrock-laws), and why static offline validation benchmarks fail to predict closed-loop physical survival (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation).
* **The Proposal-Permission Architecture**: Deconstructing the monolithic policy into an unprivileged cognitive proposer (the Brain) and a deterministic, hard real-time permission path (the Nervous System) executing Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and real-time quadratic programs on isolated safety silicon (@sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement).
* **Multi-Rate Heterogeneous Runtime Systems**: Coordinating execution across timescales spanning four orders of magnitude: semantic scene understanding at 1–5 Hz, trajectory chunking at 10–30 Hz, safety barrier filtering at 100–500 Hz, and motor inverter field-oriented control at 10–20 kHz; resolving system-on-chip (SoC) memory crossbar contention, bus arbitration jitter, and direct memory access (DMA) starvation (@sec-placement).
* **Evidence-Bound Operational Release**: Grounding system deployment claims in formal limit records, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) fault injection, residual-claims registers, and verifiable operational design domain (ODD) boundaries (@sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release, @sec-frontier).

## Curricular Reading Tracks {#sec-prereq-tracks}

To accommodate different course syllabi, research specializations, and engineering roles, this book supports four structured reading tracks:

* **Track 1: The Core Systems Curriculum (Full Sequential Arc)**:
  Designed for semester-long university courses (such as an advanced Physical AI Systems course following CS 288) and practitioners seeking complete mastery of embodied systems architecture. Traces the full four-part sequence: Foundation and Causal Boundary (@sec-boundary) $\to$ The Machine Anatomy (@sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous) $\to$ Teaching the Machine (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation) $\to$ Running the Machine (@sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement) $\to$ Governing the Machine (@sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release) $\to$ Capstone Synthesis (@sec-frontier).
* **Track 2: The ML Systems and Learned Runtimes Track (Crossing into Action)**:
  Tailored for machine learning engineers, compiler developers, and runtime researchers focusing on how high-capacity foundation models and generative action chunk decoders interface with physical execution. Emphasizes inference latency budgets, action chunking, endogenous covariate shift, closed-loop policy evaluation, runtime safety filtering, and heterogeneous SoC memory placement: @sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement, and @sec-frontier.
* **Track 3: The Silicon, RTOS, and Embedded Systems Track (Deterministic Real-Time Heterogeneity)**:
  Tailored for computer architects, embedded systems engineers, and silicon designers managing multi-rate execution across heterogeneous SoCs and real-time microcontrollers. Emphasizes physical plant dynamics, deterministic fieldbuses (CAN-FD, EtherCAT), real-time operating system (RTOS) scheduling and timer jitter, high-speed sensor transport (MIPI CSI-2, SerDes), unified memory bus contention, and safety microcontroller isolation: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement, and @sec-verification.
* **Track 4: The Robotics, Controls, and Safety Assurance Track (Certifiable Embodied Autonomy)**:
  Tailored for roboticists, control engineers, and safety certifiers integrating stochastic neural proposers into safety-critical physical plants. Emphasizes rigid-body mechanics, foundation model proposers, Control Barrier Functions, bumpless supervisory handovers, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) fault injection, empirical safety cases, and residual risk registers: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release, and @sec-frontier.

These structured tracks complement the sequential curriculum, allowing readers and instructors to navigate this book according to their primary analytical focus while maintaining full architectural context.

## What the Book Introduces

The book starts from the physical and computational relationships needed to explain a system's behavior. Specialized concepts enter through the problems they help solve, with their assumptions and limits made explicit:

* **The Proposal-Permission Separation**: Structuring the machine so high-capacity, stochastic neural networks act as unprivileged proposers, while an independent, deterministic permission path on isolated silicon validates, modifies, or rejects every action proposal before execution.
* **Unified Physical Budgets**: Unifying computational latency, sensor exposure times, bus transport delay, actuator dynamics, and Coulomb friction into a single stopping budget where delay translates directly into physical distance.
* **Multi-Rate Heterogeneous Runtime Systems**: Coordinating execution across timescales spanning four orders of magnitude: semantic scene understanding (1–5 Hz), trajectory generation (10–30 Hz), safety filtering (100–500 Hz), and motor inverter field-oriented control (10–20 kHz).
* **Endogenous Dynamics and Closed-Loop Stability**: Formulating training, data collection, and evaluation for systems whose own actions dictate future observations, addressing compounding imitation error and distribution shift.
* **Evidence-Bound Operational Release**: Grounding system deployment claims in formal limit records and empirical evidence rather than statistical extrapolation or unverified assumptions.

Detailed proofs, specialized notation, and implementation layouts provide optional depth in the appendices. The main text retains the physical mechanism, underlying assumptions, and engineering consequences so that following the systems argument does not depend on prior specialist training.

## How to Read the Numbers {#sec-reader-numbers}

Every number in this book carries one of five labels, four categories of evidence and one for design choices, and its label decides what it may be used for:

* **Measured**: A calibrated observation of a particular machine. It names its instrument, its operating conditions, its sample count, and, for a distribution, the percentile it reports. Only a measured number, or a number derived from measured ones, can support a safety margin.
* **Derived**: Computed from measured numbers through a stated physical or statistical model. It carries that model's assumptions and the propagated uncertainty of its inputs.
* **Datasheet**: A manufacturer's rating under the manufacturer's conditions. It says what to expect and what to test, and it is not evidence about the unit on the bench.
* **Illustrative**: Selected to show arithmetic or scaling. It supports no margin, timeout, or release decision.

A budget or requirement, such as a lease duration or a clearance margin, belongs to none of the four. It is a design decision, labeled **chosen**, and it means something only when it is checked against the measured or derived number it must fit, as a chosen lease is checked against the derived ceiling on pre-brake delay.

A worked design in this book shows a decision procedure. When its inputs are illustrative, the decision it reaches is illustrative too. It shows how the machine's speed, lease, or verdict would be set, and it would bind a real machine only after the inputs it names are measured.

When a number decides something, such as a speed limit, a timeout, or a release, the book keeps it as a **limit record** with six elements: the value or distribution; the operating conditions under which it holds (payload, temperature, supply voltage, surface, concurrent workload, firmware); the measurement uncertainty; the engineering margin between the operating target and the breakdown threshold; the detector that catches an excursion while the machine runs; and its provenance, meaning its label and the instrument or model that produced it. A limit holds only under its stated conditions. When wear, heat, a new payload, or a new build changes them, the limit must be established again before it is reused.

Worked examples label each number's category once, at first use. A result holds under the assumptions stated with its example and nowhere else. A bound from finitely many trials holds under its sampling assumptions and proves nothing beyond them, and a measured percentile describes the tested workload, not a worst case. In a release argument each premise also has a status: established (measured or derived), assumed, decided by accountable judgment, unsupported, or outside the threat model. @Sec-release and @sec-frontier use these statuses.

## What We Deliberately Omit

The book focuses on how learned computation, physical mechanisms, and execution systems work together. That focus limits the depth of its treatment in neighboring fields:

* **Exhaustive Robotic Kinematic Derivations**: We do not derive symbolic Denavit-Hartenberg parameter tables or catalog forward and inverse kinematics for dozens of specialized manipulator geometries. The relevant systems concern is how degrees of freedom, kinematic reach, and actuator torque limits constrain the physical workspace and stopping envelope.
* **Abstract Deep Learning Optimization Theory**: We do not explore loss surface geometry, theoretical generalization bounds, or speculative convergence proofs. Machine learning mechanisms are examined where their computational structure, memory footprint, or sampling latency directly binds the real-time execution budget.
* **Transient Software Framework and Middleware Tutorials**: We do not provide user tutorials for specific robotics middleware packages or proprietary simulation environments. Software is treated through its underlying systems primitives: zero-copy ring buffers, inter-process communication (IPC), shared-memory mailboxes, clock synchronization protocols, and DMA engines that any production runtime must manage.

These boundaries leave the essential mechanisms and their consequences in the systems argument. They limit exhaustive specialist treatment without making familiarity with that treatment a prerequisite for following the book.
